task.title: Creating Parent Pages
task.shortdesc: Learn how to create style templates for your InDesign project using parent pages.

prereq.p: Before creating a parent page, complete the following:

ul.li: Assemble the text, images, and other content needed for your project.
Configure the document settings for your desired page size and number of pages.

step.cmd: Open the Pages panel from the menu bar: Window Pages .
In the upper-right corner of the panel, click the panel menu icon with 4 horizontal lines.
Select New Parent… from the menu.
In the New Parent dialog box, enter a prefix letter. Use A for the first parent page, B for the second, and so on.
Enter a name for the parent page.
After verifying the page size and orientation, click OK.

note.p: When the parent page is created successfully, it appears in the Pages panel with the specified prefix and name.

step.cmd: In the Pages panel, double-click the parent page thumbnail to open it in your workspace.
Open the Margins and Columns dialog box: Layout Margins and Columns .
Set the desired margins and number of columns.
Set the spacing between columns (the gutter width).

steps.note: Margins should be at least 0.5 inches on all sides.

step.cmd: Select Preview to view the column guides as you adjust the settings.
After verifying the layout, click OK.

tip.p:
Use a gutter width of approximately:
0.25 inches for 2–3 columns
0.20 inches for 4 columns
For additional columns, continue decreasing the gutter width.

result.p: Purple column guides appear on the parent page. Use these guides to place text frames, image frames, and background elements.

step.cmd: In the Pages panel, select the parent page thumbnail.
Drag the parent page thumbnail onto a document page thumbnail.
Release the mouse button when a black rectangle appears around the document page thumbnail.
Repeat steps 2 and 3 to apply the parent page to the remaining pages in the section.

section.title: Next Steps
section.p: You can now place text and images consistently throughout the document. To apply different layouts to specific sections, create additional parent pages and apply them to the appropriate pages.
